title: Inside orch
subtitle: Building and Operating a Docker Orchestrator in Go
author: Aleksandar Popovic
delivery_status: Complete generation plan; manuscript not yet generated

chapters.title: Why Build a Container Orchestrator?
chapters.focus: Define the small-cluster problem, desired-state architecture, and the project’s verified implementation boundary.
learning_objectives: Trace a service from API request to Docker container.
Separate project intent from default binary behavior.
Explain when a small orchestrator is an appropriate engineering choice.
chapters.lab: Draw the Atlas Lab system map and record the pinned source revision.
chapters.quality_contract: Every capability claim has a source classification; MemoryService is named explicitly and the architecture map does not imply PostgreSQL server integration.

chapters.title: A Repository Built for Reasoning
chapters.focus: Read package boundaries, interfaces, injected dependencies, cancellation rules, and the repository’s engineering contract.
learning_objectives: Navigate the actual package tree.
Identify side-effect boundaries and dependency injection.
Use deterministic tests and context cancellation as design constraints.
chapters.lab: Create a read-only source index and run the prerequisite and build checks.
chapters.quality_contract: Show actual package names rather than copying intended AGENTS layout; explain why internal/docker and internal/health differ from planned directory names.

chapters.title: Boot the Lab and Deploy the First Service
chapters.focus: Run the pinned local development path and inspect CLI-visible service, task, and node state.
learning_objectives: Build or install the pinned CLI reproducibly.
Start and tear down the local cluster.
Read service and task state after deployment.
chapters.lab: Deploy the upstream http-api example, inspect events, scale, collect logs, then remove it.
chapters.quality_contract: All commands are checked against current CLI behavior; document Docker requirements, port prerequisites, and cleanup; do not invent output transcripts.

chapters.title: Domain Models and State Machines
chapters.focus: Study service, task, node, deployment, and event types as explicit contracts.
learning_objectives: Distinguish desired task status from observed status.
Explain valid and invalid lifecycle transitions.
Relate immutable service versions to deployments.
chapters.lab: Trace Atlas API lifecycle transitions with a state transition table and one rejected transition test.
chapters.quality_contract: The diagram includes terminal states and transition ownership; every shown state exists in pinned types and invalid transitions have evidence.

chapters.title: Service Specifications, Resources, and Ports
chapters.focus: Read declarative service validation, resource quantities, labels, and host-port allocation constraints.
learning_objectives: Parse CPU and memory quantities without ambiguity.
Describe requested resources and placement constraints.
Predict a public-port collision and validation error.
chapters.lab: Create good and deliberately invalid Atlas manifests; explain replicas versus finite host-port capacity.
chapters.quality_contract: Resource arithmetic includes units; published host ports are node-scoped; invalid manifests are tested through the actual parser.

chapters.title: Follow One Request Through the Control Plane
chapters.focus: Walk the default server assembly, in-memory control plane, controller loops, and runtime integration gaps.
learning_objectives: Locate the actual control-plane constructor.
Explain how API mutations and controller iterations interact.
Identify state that is lost on a default server restart.
chapters.lab: Restart the local server in a disposable lab and contrast surviving Docker containers with lost control-plane state.
chapters.quality_contract: Trace current call sites; do not claim DB URL configuration enables persistent server state; classify restart observations as measured or expected.

chapters.title: HTTP Contracts and Compatible APIs
chapters.focus: Study middleware, validation, stable error responses, versioned routes, and the shared API contract.
learning_objectives: Follow validation and authorization at the HTTP boundary.
Map domain errors to stable client-facing errors.
Check OpenAPI documentation against route behavior.
chapters.lab: Call the API with valid and invalid requests and add a book-side contract smoke test using the public client.
chapters.quality_contract: OpenAPI versus route gaps go into the contradiction ledger; public and internal agent contracts remain distinct; additive compatibility is demonstrated.

chapters.title: A CLI That Operators Can Automate
chapters.focus: Explore Cobra command composition, configuration precedence, JSON output, and deployment parsing.
learning_objectives: Explain flag, environment, configuration, and default precedence.
Use stable JSON output for a small automation script.
Distinguish local validation from server-side acceptance.
chapters.lab: Write an Atlas status script that uses current JSON fields and reports actionable failures.
chapters.quality_contract: Run the exact illustrated commands; do not introduce unsupported switches; examples redact tokens and do not assume an implicit server URL.

chapters.title: Persistence, Transactions, and Optimistic Concurrency
chapters.focus: Read PostgreSQL store interfaces and transactions while distinguishing them from the default in-memory server.
learning_objectives: Identify transaction boundaries and optimistic conflict checks.
Explain store integration test isolation.
Distinguish persisted schemas from integrated production durability.
chapters.lab: Run store integration tests against a disposable PostgreSQL database and examine a conflicting write.
chapters.quality_contract: Database tests may reapply down/up migrations and require disposable data; show actual transaction code; server wiring stays an explicitly separate architectural exercise.

chapters.title: A Deterministic Scheduler
chapters.focus: Read placement order, eligibility checks, capacity accounting, and concurrent assignment safety.
learning_objectives: Explain deterministic ordering and tie-breaking.
Check labels, status, resources, ports, and storage topology.
Identify the persistence conflict path during assignment.
chapters.lab: Build a tiny fake-node placement experiment with valid, exhausted, and conflicting nodes.
chapters.quality_contract: Calculate one complete placement by hand and confirm with a test; task assignment is unique; resource and port claims are not described as Docker enforcement.

chapters.title: Reconciliation as Repeated Convergence
chapters.focus: Explain creation, scale-down, restart policy, soft deletion, and restart idempotency.
learning_objectives: Separate reconciliation decisions from placement and runtime side effects.
Demonstrate repeated RunOnce convergence.
Handle failed tasks and service soft deletion.
chapters.lab: Apply the same desired Atlas replica count repeatedly in deterministic tests and verify no duplicate tasks.
chapters.quality_contract: Show what each repeated iteration reads and writes; account for transitional tasks; document the default server’s actual invocation path rather than assuming a wired standalone loop.

chapters.title: Idempotent Docker Operations and Drift
chapters.focus: Study the typed Docker adapter, managed labels, fake runtime, cleanup boundaries, and external container drift.
learning_objectives: Identify idempotency keys and managed-container labels.
Explain how repeated create/start/remove calls converge.
Separate unmanaged containers from safe cleanup candidates.
chapters.lab: Repeat runtime operations through FakeRuntime and inject a missing or manually stopped managed container.
chapters.quality_contract: Use actual Runtime methods and labels; drift repair respects task identity; no example removes unrelated host containers.

chapters.title: Agents, Heartbeats, and Task Reports
chapters.focus: Trace registration, heartbeat, polling, local reconciliation, and status reporting.
learning_objectives: Follow agent bootstrap and credential use.
Explain agent versus server decision ownership.
Interpret repeated task reports and heartbeat failure.
chapters.lab: Observe one Atlas worker agent and simulate dropped reports using deterministic fakes.
chapters.quality_contract: Task status updates are grounded in request types; explain retry and cancellation behavior without implying exactly-once delivery or mTLS.

chapters.title: Health Checks That Respect Trust Boundaries
chapters.focus: Read HTTP/TCP health checks, timeout behavior, status transitions, and SSRF controls.
learning_objectives: Distinguish process running from healthy service state.
Explain timeout, retry, and health reporting semantics.
Demonstrate allowed and rejected probe targets.
chapters.lab: Inject healthy, timeout, and forbidden-target probes for Atlas API without contacting metadata services.
chapters.quality_contract: SSRF examples use fake network/probe boundaries; capture actual allow/deny conditions and acknowledge remaining host-network risks.

chapters.title: Events, Audits, and Notification Boundaries
chapters.focus: Treat events as operator history, audit as an attribution record, and notifications as external effects.
learning_objectives: Differentiate domain events, diagnostic logs, and audits.
Trace redaction and actor attribution.
Explain notification delivery, retry, and failure isolation from code.
chapters.lab: Capture the Atlas deployment event timeline and send notifications to a local fake sink.
chapters.quality_contract: Do not equate the default memory-backed event history with durable production events; delivery guarantees and redaction claims come from implementation tests.

chapters.title: Log Streaming Without Losing Control
chapters.focus: Trace server-to-agent log paths, Docker stream framing, cancellation, and bounded operator consumption.
learning_objectives: Locate actual log stream boundaries and response formats.
Explain tail, follow, cancellation, and transport errors.
Separate orchestration events from application stdout/stderr.
chapters.lab: Stream Atlas application logs, disconnect the client, and check cancellation through a local test.
chapters.quality_contract: Use actual agent/API/runtime log files; explain cancellation and stream errors; never fabricate a centralized persistent log collector.

chapters.title: Rolling Updates and Rollback Invariants
chapters.focus: Explore service versions, deployment locks, max surge, max unavailable, and rollback state machines.
learning_objectives: Compute rollout availability and surge limits.
Explain failed target versions and previous successful versions.
Reject conflicting user mutations during a deployment.
chapters.lab: Roll Atlas API forward, inject an unhealthy target, and trace a rollback in fake and optional Docker lab modes.
chapters.quality_contract: Include invariant arithmetic and one failure timeline; no zero-downtime guarantee exceeds tested health and routing behavior.

chapters.title: Safe Deletion and Resource Cleanup
chapters.focus: Follow deleting versus deleted services, task stop/remove behavior, finalization, and failures.
learning_objectives: Explain why removal is a workflow rather than one HTTP delete.
Trace cleanup ownership and retry behavior.
Identify resource leaks and safe finalization conditions.
chapters.lab: Delete Atlas API while injecting one remove failure; inspect repeated cleanup attempts.
chapters.quality_contract: Distinguish desired deletion from confirmed runtime removal; demonstrate repeated calls and avoid destructive force-cleanup recipes.

chapters.title: Offline Nodes, Draining, and Rescheduling
chapters.focus: Read heartbeat expiry, node statuses, drain/uncordon operations, and workload rescheduling safety.
learning_objectives: Interpret stale heartbeat transitions.
Explain why drain differs from immediate node deletion.
Reason about replacement tasks and partition uncertainty.
chapters.lab: Pause a disposable Atlas agent and perform a deterministic drain/reschedule trace.
chapters.quality_contract: Correct stale docs that call node monitoring unimplemented; include a partition case and clearly identify what orch cannot fence on an isolated worker.

chapters.title: Endpoint Discovery and Internal DNS
chapters.focus: Study endpoint filtering, namespace names, host addresses and published ports, DNS TTL, and unhealthy endpoints.
learning_objectives: Explain endpoint identity and health filtering.
Distinguish DNS names from stable virtual IPs.
Reason about stale caches and rescheduled endpoints.
chapters.lab: Query Atlas endpoints and internal DNS under healthy and unhealthy fake task states.
chapters.quality_contract: Explain DNS returns node addresses and clients still need ports; no Kubernetes compatibility, overlay, VIP, or automatic cross-node networking claim.

chapters.title: Ingress, Host Networking, and the Overlay Roadmap
chapters.focus: Read Traefik configuration and current host-port traffic flow before evaluating future overlay/CNI design.
learning_objectives: Trace ingress to node-level published ports.
Identify collisions, topology exposure, and routing limitations.
Evaluate an overlay/CNI design without claiming it is built.
chapters.lab: Route Atlas API with the upstream Traefik example and draw the current packet path.
chapters.quality_contract: Separate executable ingress examples from design-only overlay/CNI; show actual router/service fields and a failure path.

chapters.title: Autoscaling Decisions and Missing Integration
chapters.focus: Read CPU recommendations, bounds, cooldown, rollout exclusion, and production provider gaps.
learning_objectives: Calculate a replica recommendation from observed CPU.
Explain bounded scaling and cooldown.
Identify the missing production metrics provider and default-server wiring.
chapters.lab: Drive Atlas replica recommendations with FakeMetricsProvider and inspect cooldown behavior.
chapters.quality_contract: Do not assert automatic production autoscaling is active; distinguish declared stabilizationWindow from enforced behavior and state whether cooldown is durable.

chapters.title: Authentication, Authorization, and Node Trust
chapters.focus: Study operator JWT roles, agent enrollment tokens, route authorization, and node trust limits.
learning_objectives: Distinguish user authentication from agent bootstrap.
Trace role checks for sensitive operations.
Explain Docker socket privilege and missing mTLS identity.
chapters.lab: Run Atlas API authorization tests with viewer, operator, admin, and invalid agent credentials.
chapters.quality_contract: Use placeholder credentials only; document auth enablement and actual defaults; no claim token authentication is equivalent to mutual TLS.

chapters.title: Encrypted Secrets and Configuration Redaction
chapters.focus: Read secret envelope construction, namespace reference resolution, configuration precedence, and redacted output.
learning_objectives: Trace secret encrypt/decrypt and reference resolution.
Explain local key custody and rotation gaps.
Check diagnostic paths for redaction.
chapters.lab: Deploy an Atlas placeholder-secret example and assert sample sensitive values are absent from printed configuration.
chapters.quality_contract: Do not promise external KMS or rotation not implemented; examples never put real secrets in command arguments or committed files.

chapters.title: Registry Credentials and Immutable Image Identity
chapters.focus: Connect registry authentication, image references, tag policy, and digest pinning to rollout traceability.
learning_objectives: Parse tags and digests through actual image-reference code.
Trace namespace-scoped registry credentials.
Explain mutable-tag risk and the implemented pinning policy.
chapters.lab: Validate Atlas image references and use an explicitly labeled placeholder digest for non-executing examples.
chapters.quality_contract: Use real verified digest only for executable labs; classify fake digests as explanatory; image signing is reserved for the design chapter.

chapters.title: Security Contexts, Admission, and Policy
chapters.focus: Read enforceable container security fields and policy/admission entry points.
learning_objectives: Distinguish supported security context fields from host isolation.
Explain admission sequencing and rejection evidence.
Verify CLI, API, and GitOps share policy acceptance boundaries.
chapters.lab: Reject an unsafe Atlas manifest and inspect stable policy error details.
chapters.quality_contract: Do not imply a sandbox beyond Docker enforcement; supported admission hooks are code-evidenced and external policy-engine concepts remain proposals.

chapters.title: Namespaces and the Limits of Multi-Tenancy
chapters.focus: Study namespace context, 404 isolation behavior, namespace-local uniqueness, role maps, and shared host risks.
learning_objectives: Resolve namespaces consistently across API and CLI.
Show cross-namespace secret and object isolation.
Explain why logical namespaces are not a hostile-tenant security boundary.
chapters.lab: Deploy two Atlas API services with the same name in different namespaces and verify invisible cross-namespace IDs.
chapters.quality_contract: Every isolation guarantee is scoped; discuss shared nodes, Docker and networking; down-migration data loss is explicit in the appendix runbook.

chapters.title: Quotas and Usage Accounting
chapters.focus: Read atomic quota checks, requested resource accounting, usage snapshots, and operational exports.
learning_objectives: Calculate namespace requested CPU/memory and port usage.
Explain concurrent quota enforcement and zero-as-unlimited.
Distinguish operational usage reports from invoices or payment billing.
chapters.lab: Exhaust an Atlas namespace quota and export a bounded usage report with known dimensions.
chapters.quality_contract: State whether each guarantee comes from MemoryService or PostgreSQL store; CSV units are documented; no complete billing product claim.

chapters.title: Supply Chain Designs Without False Guarantees
chapters.focus: Analyze image signing, SBOM and vulnerability scanning proposals against implemented image-policy boundaries.
learning_objectives: Separate digest identity from signature authenticity.
Design a verification and provenance decision path.
Define fail-open/fail-closed and scanner freshness tradeoffs.
chapters.lab: Write an Atlas threat model and a book-side verification contract; mark every proposed adapter as illustrative.
chapters.quality_contract: Signing and scanning are design material unless implementation evidence proves otherwise; do not install moving external tools without official versioned references.

chapters.title: GitOps, Drift, and Controlled Reconciliation
chapters.focus: Trace isolated git checkout, manifest parse/admission, recorded revision, warn/auto-revert drift, and prune ownership.
learning_objectives: Explain source revision provenance and deterministic manifest order.
Contrast warn and auto_revert drift behavior.
Bound pruning to the source’s managed services.
chapters.lab: Use a local Atlas manifest repository, introduce manual drift, and demonstrate warn versus auto_revert.
chapters.quality_contract: Use a real local committed revision; no userinfo credentials in URLs; illustrate failure isolation and ensure prune never touches unrelated services.

chapters.title: Finite Jobs and Time-Based Work
chapters.focus: Read Job attempts, retry limits, CronJob parsing, timezone semantics, concurrency policies, and missed runs.
learning_objectives: Trace Job exit status to success, failure, or retry.
Explain Allow, Forbid, and Replace concurrency.
Reason about timezone and bounded missed occurrences.
chapters.lab: Run a finite Atlas report job and drive CronJob fake time through overlap and missed-occurrence cases.
chapters.quality_contract: Use exact supported five-field cron syntax and workload YAML; UTC and timezone cases are explicit; do not claim exactly-once scheduling.

chapters.title: Local Volumes, Claims, and Workload Topology
chapters.focus: Study local volume claims, scheduler topology, active writer locks, attachment lifecycle, and unsupported distributed storage.
learning_objectives: Explain why a local claim binds future placement to a node.
Trace writer-lock and read-only attachment behavior.
Separate storage metadata safety from data replication and backup.
chapters.lab: Attach a disposable Atlas local volume and reject a second writer or wrong-node placement in tests.
chapters.quality_contract: Do not portray RWO as distributed fencing; no replicated stateful-service promise; cleanup requires explicit data retention choices.

chapters.title: Extension Interfaces and a Plugin Roadmap
chapters.focus: Read existing side-effect interfaces and design external RPC plugin lifecycle without inventing a plugin implementation.
learning_objectives: Identify present runtime, secrets, metrics, and notification seams.
Design versioned handshake and capability negotiation.
Analyze least privilege, cancellation, crash isolation, and idempotency.
chapters.lab: Create an Atlas adapter contract exercise and label the external RPC protocol as a design proposal.
chapters.quality_contract: Separate existing interfaces from design-only supervisors and RPC; no arbitrary code-loading sample; contract pseudocode is clearly labeled and not presented as upstream source.

chapters.title: Leader Election and the Durable HA Boundary
chapters.focus: Study lease interfaces, PostgreSQL advisory locks, leadership cancellation, and the default server integration gap.
learning_objectives: Explain per-controller leadership versus API availability.
Trace lease loss to controller cancellation.
Evaluate PostgreSQL connection and dual-primary failure assumptions.
chapters.lab: Run deterministic competing-leader tests and draft a separate durable-server wiring ADR for Atlas.
chapters.quality_contract: Do not launch multiple default MemoryService servers as HA; advisory lock packages do not imply production wiring; include partition and leadership loss scenarios.

chapters.title: Upgrades, Migrations, Maintenance, and Retention
chapters.focus: Read version compatibility, safe migration locks, down guards, maintenance windows, and bounded retention.
learning_objectives: Read current server, agent, API, and schema compatibility ranges.
Explain migration checks and guarded rollback.
Apply maintenance and retention policies with preservation boundaries.
chapters.lab: Perform a disposable Atlas migration-status and upgrade-preflight exercise, then dry-run retention.
chapters.quality_contract: All schema ranges are pinned to source version; show ORCH_SCHEMA_CHECK enablement from main.go instead of implying unconditional checks; never test down migrations on real data.

chapters.title: Fakes, Property Tests, Fuzzing, and Contracts
chapters.focus: Use existing deterministic fakes, seeded scheduler properties, fuzz targets, and E2E tests as executable specifications.
learning_objectives: Select the smallest test boundary that proves an invariant.
Reproduce a seeded property failure.
Preserve fuzz findings as minimal regression cases.
chapters.lab: Add book-side exercises for duplicate placement, parser panic resistance, and repeated convergence.
chapters.quality_contract: No mirrored tests that simply restate implementation; fuzz duration and manual CI policy are explicit; skipped integration tests are recorded rather than counted as passed.

chapters.title: Failure Injection and Recovery Evidence
chapters.focus: Turn failure-mode hardening and chaos scenarios into bounded recovery investigations.
learning_objectives: Define an invariant before injecting a fault.
Distinguish timeout, runtime failure, node loss, and partition.
Measure convergence and identify unsupported recovery guarantees.
chapters.lab: Run Atlas failure drills with fake runtime faults and optional local process interruption.
chapters.quality_contract: Every drill specifies fault, expected behavior, observations, recovery, and cleanup; do not mistake fake-system success for distributed production resilience.

chapters.title: Metrics, Dashboards, and Actionable Signals
chapters.focus: Trace Prometheus instruments, cardinality, alert rules, dashboard panels, and links to operator actions.
learning_objectives: Map an emitted metric to a subsystem and failure mode.
Explain counters, gauges, labels, and cardinality cost.
Connect an alert to a concrete investigation.
chapters.lab: Inspect Atlas metrics and validate one real alert expression and dashboard query against emitted metric names.
chapters.quality_contract: Metric names and PromQL are copied from pinned source; dashboard mismatches are reported; no invented SLO, recording rule, or benchmark chart.

chapters.title: Performance and Scale Tests That Say What They Measure
chapters.focus: Read fake-agent load tests, scheduler/API benchmarks, pprof controls, and large-service stress scenarios.
learning_objectives: Separate fake control-plane throughput from real Docker capacity.
Record hardware, commit, seed, flags, and measurement uncertainty.
Profile only on protected debug surfaces.
chapters.lab: Run a bounded Atlas benchmark and create a measured-results template without fabricated data.
chapters.quality_contract: A 1,000-service fake-agent scenario is not a production capacity claim; pprof exposure controls are source-checked; all numbers are measured or explicitly hypothetical.

chapters.title: Release a System You Can Honestly Operate
chapters.focus: Bring together reproducible release checks, deployment manifests, recovery drills, readiness limits, and an evidence-based production backlog.
learning_objectives: Verify build/test/lint/release contracts and distinguish skipped checks.
Explain what PostgreSQL backup does and does not restore for default MemoryService.
Produce a source-grounded readiness review and next-step ADRs.
chapters.lab: Assemble Atlas evidence: tested lab, unresolved gaps, backup drill, compatibility preflight, and publication-ready case study.
chapters.quality_contract: Final checklist cannot override MemoryService, missing HA/autoscaler wiring, mTLS, and networking gaps; title/subtitle and product copy never claim production readiness.

appendices.title: CLI, API, and Configuration Reference
appendices.focus: Produce a source-derived command, route, field and configuration reference.
learning_objectives: Provide tested command sequences and a compact environment matrix.
appendices.lab: Reset a disposable Atlas lab without deleting unrelated Docker data.
appendices.quality_contract: Every cleanup command is scoped; source version, architecture, Docker availability, and skipped checks are recorded.

appendices.title: Lifecycle States and Invariant Reference
appendices.focus: Define lifecycle states, transitions, ownership and concurrency invariants.
learning_objectives: Cross-check every field and switch against parser and CLI definitions.
appendices.quality_contract: Defaults and supported spellings come from current source; reference examples include both success and rejection.

appendices.title: Commit Atlas and Original Prompt Crosswalk
appendices.focus: Explain the 91 original prompts and real implementation associations across 105 commits.
learning_objectives: Separate semantic matches, ambiguous matches, tracking commits, and later amendments.
appendices.lab: Open immutable commit and blob links from the evidence ledger.
appendices.quality_contract: Full commit SHA and file anchors only; prompt completion is intent evidence rather than proof; unmapped items remain visible.

appendices.title: Worked Exercises and Design Solutions
appendices.focus: Collect tested and source-justified answers keyed to chapters and labs.
learning_objectives: Link each concept to a concrete orch behavior or an explicitly proposed extension.
appendices.lab: Write Atlas ADRs for durable store wiring, leadership, and networking.
appendices.quality_contract: Do not attribute general distributed-systems guarantees to orch without code and test proof.

appendices.title: Operator Runbooks and Measurement Contracts
appendices.focus: Provide observable triage, backup boundary, migration, maintenance and measurement procedures.
learning_objectives: Pair every operation with preconditions, observation, abort criteria, and cleanup.
appendices.lab: Complete one Atlas incident worksheet and restore drill.
appendices.quality_contract: No production runbook suggests restart-safe default control-plane state; irreversible down/restore operations require explicit disposable lab boundaries.

appendices.title: Glossary, Bibliography, and Boundary Index
appendices.focus: Define technical terms and primary references; link the capability/extension backlog.
learning_objectives: Classify implemented-and-wired, implemented-package-only, design-only, and verified absence separately.
appendices.lab: Prioritize Atlas extension ADRs by risk and prerequisites.
appendices.quality_contract: Use pinned code as authority when docs conflict; all extensions are proposals and no hidden patch to orch is implied.
